hints: Making the array nondecreasing raises each value to the maximum previously seen.
For a query range, each position's required increase depends on the prefix maximum before it.
Group positions by the next greater-or-equal value and use prefix sums to sum the repeated target-minus-value costs.
analogy: As you scan a range, each low item is lifted to the tallest earlier item.
example: For [3,1,2], adjusted values are [3,3,3], so increases total 3.
algorithm: Build next-greater links and prefix sums; for each range, jump between blocks sharing the same prefix maximum and compute their total increments from prefix sums.
correctness: The monotone transformation sets each position to the maximum of the range prefix through that position, which is exactly the least nondecreasing value sequence dominating the input.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time with binary lifting and prefix sums; O(n log n) space.
